To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the tTG promoter is activated in vivo during glucocorticoid-induced apoptosis, (ii) this activation is not observed in vitro, (iii) the tTG gene promoter is activated in endocrine apoptosis, (iv) the tTG reporter gene is activated in vivo in tissues with high apoptotic turnover, and (v) the tTG activation is not observed when the reporter gene is expressed in the absence of the endogenous gene.
the apoptosis-specific regulation of the tissue-specific tTG gene promoter is mediated by a 3.9 kb fragment and may require additional factors available only in vivo.
the tTG promoter is regulated by apoptotic stimuli.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of the tTG gene in apoptosis and may contribute to the understanding of the role of tTG in cell survival and apoptosis.
the identification of the regulatory elements involved in the apoptotic activation of the tTG gene.
the transcriptional regulation and the biological function of tissue transglutaminate in apoptosis and tissue remodelling.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the tTG gene is a marker for apoptotic cells in vivo.
the regulation of tTG transcription is linked to the apoptotic process and is controlled by a 3.5 kb promoter fragment in vivo.
the regulation of tTG transcription by apoptosis is mediated via a complex network of regulatory elements, which may include a promoter and a tissue-specific element.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the tTG gene promoter is a target for apoptosis-specific transcription factors.
the tTG promoter contains a regulatory element(s) that is activated in vivo during apoptosis.

the tTG promoter contains elements that are activated during apoptosis and in vivo, but not in vitro, and that the in vivo induction of the transgene may be dependent on additional signals present in tissue environment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the transgene construct is a good model to study tTG transcriptional control in vivo.
the tTG promoter can be used to monitor in vivo apoptosis in a variety of experimental settings.
the tTG promoter is a good model for the study of transcriptional regulation of apoptosis.
